topLevel.why: X follows the document's major divisions, including separate Notation and Bibliography parts. Y welds Notation into the Preface and the Bibliography into Historic Perspective; neither tree cuts a chapter partway through.

gists.why: X more accurately locates and describes the Fourier-to-graph passage and gives more targeted accounts of RNN shift equivariance and the history of mesh spectral methods. Y is better on the introductory learning principles and object recognition, but its GNN gist makes a stronger expressiveness claim than the passage supports.

weldedParts.why: Combines the completed conceptual preface with the separately headed mathematical notation reference.
Includes the separately headed Bibliography after the historical discussion and acknowledgements.

inventedClaims.what: Claims that each successive GNN flavour is strictly more expressive and harder to scale; the passage describes fixed-weight convolutional aggregation and spectral filters without establishing that strict hierarchy.
Attributes surpassing human performance broadly to architectures including AlexNet and VGG-16, while the passage supports advances in object detection and segmentation, not that performance claim.

overall.why: X preserves the document's major divisions and provides the more reliable section map overall. Its more specific gists also better guide readers to several of the technical passages.
